title: Add benchmark regression budgets and CI summary checks
description:
Problem: MemorySmith has BenchmarkDotNet search benchmarks and NUnit search-quality probes, but CI does not compare current runs against explicit performance budgets or historical baselines. Performance regressions can therefore appear only as anecdotal local observations.

Desired outcome: critical flows have explicit report-only or enforced performance budgets, and CI/local validation emits a concise benchmark summary that shows whether search/context/page/chat latency changed enough to investigate.

Scope:
- In scope: define initial budgets for search/context-pack benchmark smoke paths, add a repeatable summary command, store or compare against baseline data where practical, and document which budgets are blocking versus report-only.
- Out of scope: optimizing individual slow operations unless the new budget check exposes a confirmed regression.

Dependencies:
- Coordinate with TSK-0108 benchmark trace events and TSK-0069 CI topology.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least one critical benchmark path has a documented budget and machine-readable summary output.
- CI or local validation reports benchmark status without requiring a full long-running BenchmarkDotNet suite on every PR.
- Budget failures or warnings include enough metadata to reproduce locally.

Validation:
- Run the benchmark smoke command and capture summary output.
- Run the new budget/report command twice and verify stable comparison behavior.
- Confirm CI summary output is readable and does not fail on missing optional ONNX model assets unless that gate is explicitly enabled.

Rollback:
- Convert blocking budgets to report-only while retaining summaries if early budgets are too noisy.

Risks:
- Hardware variance can make strict latency thresholds flaky unless budgets are conservative or trend-based.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from ultra audit findings F-007 and F-008. Evidence: benchmark commands and search-quality probes exist, but .github/workflows/ci.yml has no benchmark budget comparison lane.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: 2026-08-08 deep-dive observed hybrid benchmark latency 434 ms against a hard-coded 300 ms budget. Separate correctness from performance, use warm-up/percentile baselines, and avoid making machine variance look like relevance failure.
